title: Introduce per-layer scale-LUT INT8 attention path with fragmented dequant merge and KV-adaptive windowing
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: reduce per-token CPU/GPU overhead for INT8 attention while preserving numerical stability across diverse model families and sequence lengths. We observed a recurring cost hotspot in the dequant->scale->attn kernel boundary when using per-layer static scales; scale reapplication and memory traffic dominated token-cost for medium-length sequences. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) a compact per-layer scale lookup-table (scale-LUT) used at kernel boundaries to avoid repeated wide-vector scale multiplications; 2) a fragmented-dequant merge that fuses small contiguous dequant regions into the attention microkernel to eliminate an intermediate buffer copy for common prefix sizes; 3) an adaptive KV cache windowing heuristic that short-circuits KV read for very recent prefixes and improves cache locality for long context runs. Work items and checklist: - implement scale-LUT map and fast path in attn microkernel - fused fragmented-dequant path (kernel-level) and small-copy fallback - KV-adaptive window policy + tunable thresholds exposed to runtime config - microbatch token-affinity coalescer tweaks to pair with new kernel fast paths - add microbench harness and end-to-end eval for quantized models - safety: FP8 fallback for layers flagged with near-underflow/overflow histograms Related: ENG-17892 (quant rollout), ENG-17911 (kv-window policy). Design notes: scale-LUT stores 16-bit fixed-point scale entries per layer group and is applied by a single narrow kernel that multiplies a packed int8 block using a precomputed multiplier and shift; this reduces global memory reads and avoids broadcasting a float scale tensor for every token. The fragmented-dequant merge recognises small contiguous slices (<=128 tokens) and merges the dequant into the attention input assembler so the dequant step is performed as the data is streamed into the GPU register tile. KV-adaptive windowing uses access-frequency histograms from the last N requests to dynamically shrink the KV window for hot prefixes; this improves L2 cache reuse and reduces pressure on GPU global memory for long-running chats. Benchmarks (representative): - LLAMA-2-7B, single-GPU, p50 latency (bs=1, seq=512): baseline INT8 path=43.7ms -> new path=37.1ms (~15% p50 improvement) - LLAMA-2-13B, bs=1, seq=1024: baseline=89.4ms -> new=77.3ms (~13.6%) - Throughput (bs=8, seq=256) for 7B: baseline=220 tok/s -> new=255 tok/s (~16% uplift) - Cost: token-GPU-time reduced ~12% in synthetic steady-state runs Safety/regressions: added unit tests to detect bit-exactness where applicable and quantization histogram guards; the PR includes a canary rollout in the perf-canary harness with a traffic shadow to compare outputs and triggers a rollback if per-token BLEU/ROUGE deviance > configured threshold. Migration and config: the feature is disabled by default; enable via runtime flag --quant-int8-scale-lut=true and --kv-adaptive-window=<percentile>. There is a small compatibility shim for customers using pinned model bundles that lack layer-group metadata; for those bundles the runtime falls back to current per-layer scale tensors. CI: builds, lint, unit tests, and perf-canary all passed; one flake in the initial run (random seed ordering) was fixed by seeding the microbench harness. Merge: squashed and merged to main. Notes for release: this is non-breaking by default (feature gated). Monitor token-level latency and the perf-canary dashboards for early degradations.
